q: tell me about global academy of technology
entries.a: GAT is Global Academy of Technology, an autonomous engineering and management institute in Bengaluru, affiliated to VTU. It was established in 2001 and sits on a 10-acre solar-powered green campus at Rajarajeshwari Nagar.

q: what is the vision of gat
entries.a: GAT's vision is to become a premier institution imparting quality education in engineering and management to meet the changing needs of society. Its mission is threefold: a learning environment supported by modern infrastructure, research and innovation through industry collaboration, and ethical values with environmental consciousness.
GAT was established in 2001. The campus spans over 10 acres in Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Bengaluru.
Dr. Balakrishna H. B. is the Principal of GAT. Dr. Annepu Sreedhar Kumar is the Campus Director.

GAT offers ten B.E. branches: Computer Science and Engineering, Information Science and Engineering, Artificial Intelligence and Data Science, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, CSE (AI & ML), Electronics and Communication, Electrical and Electronics, Mechanical, Civil, and Aeronautical Engineering. All are 4 years, 8 semesters.
GAT offers an MBA, M.Tech in Structural Engineering, and M.Tech in Computer Science. Postgraduate programmes run 2 years across 4 semesters.
For B.E. you need 10+2 (Karnataka State Board, CBSE or equivalent) with Physics and Mathematics, plus Chemistry, Biology or Computer Science, and a minimum of 45% marks.
For M.Tech you need a B.E. or B.Tech in a relevant field with at least 50% marks (45% for Karnataka SC/ST/OBC) and a valid PGCET or GATE score.

Undergraduate admission is through KCET for Karnataka students and COMEDK for students from outside Karnataka, or through management quota. Postgraduate admission (MBA, M.Tech) is through PGCET or GATE.

q: can students from other states apply
am i eligible from another state
can students from other states join
from another state can i apply
entries.a: Yes. Students from other states can apply through COMEDK for undergraduate courses. For postgraduate programmes, eligibility is through PGCET or management quota admissions.
Lateral entry is available for diploma holders in a relevant engineering discipline with at least 45% marks (40% for reserved categories), admitted through DCET as per Government of Karnataka norms.

Apply through KCET, COMEDK or management quota for UG, and PGCET or GATE for PG. The admissions team can walk you through documents and fees: call +91-9902463002 or +91-9243190105, or email admissions@gat.ac.in.

GAT publishes the fee breakdown (tuition, hostel and other charges) as a downloadable document in the Admissions section of gat.ac.in. For exact current figures, contact admissions@gat.ac.in or call +91-9243190105 — I don't want to quote a number that may be out of date.
GAT does list scholarships among its admissions resources. For which ones you qualify for and the current criteria, contact the admissions office at admissions@gat.ac.in or +91-9243190105.
Yes, GAT provides hostel facilities for both boys and girls. The hostels have comfortable accommodation, dining facilities, Wi-Fi, security and recreational areas.

The GAT Library and Information Center holds over 35,000 documents — 64,626 titles and 87,029 volumes — across two floors in the Annex B block, with a reference section seating 70. It runs LIBSOFT with barcode technology, and the OPAC catalogue can be searched from inside or outside campus. Digital resources are available 24/7.

GAT ranked No. 1 in the VTU Sports Rankings 2025 and has stayed in the top 5 since 2015, with 30+ national-level athletes in 2023–24. There are indoor and outdoor facilities, coaching, athletic teams and inter-college tournaments.
Campus life at GAT covers sports and physical education, cultural activities, NCC, NSS, hostel life, student clubs, student well-being and regular events.

Placements are run by the Career Counselling, Training and Placement (CCTP) department. The process runs from pre-placement planning and company outreach through aptitude and technical training, mock interviews and resume building, pre-placement talks, then online tests, group discussions and technical/HR interviews.

q: what can i do after mba
entries.a: An MBA from GAT opens opportunities in finance, marketing, human resources, operations and entrepreneurship. A dedicated placement cell supports students through campus placements, internships and industry tie-ups.

CampusCare is the campus grievance app for GAT. You photograph a problem on campus — an overflowing bin, a broken fan, a leaking tap — and it goes to the right department automatically, with AI working out the category, the priority and which team should fix it. You can then track it until it's resolved.

q: how do i report a problem
how do i tell someone about a problem
entries.a: Tap 'Report a problem' on the home screen. The camera opens, you take one photo of the issue, pick or confirm the zone, type a short description, and submit. The AI sorts out the category, priority and department — you don't fill in any forms.

q: why does it need the camera
can i submit without a photo
entries.a: Yes, a photo is part of every complaint, and it must be taken in the app rather than picked from your gallery. That's deliberate — it keeps reports genuine and current, and proves the problem is really there.

q: it says im not on campus
do i have to be on campus
outside the college can i still report
entries.a: You have to be physically inside the GAT campus to submit, and the app checks your GPS against the real campus boundary. If you're off campus it will tell you so and won't accept the complaint. If you're indoors and GPS is weak, step near a window or into the open and try again.

q: will the admin see my name
will people know it was me
will anyone know i reported it
will anyone know that i reported the issue
does the admin know who reported
entries.a: Your name is never shown to admins. Every complaint carries a random friendly alias instead — something like 'Crispy Llama' — and that privacy is enforced by the database rules, not just hidden in the app. Staff see the problem, the place and the alias, never who reported it.
Open 'My Complaints' from the bottom bar. Each one shows a live status timeline — Submitted, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved — and updates as the department works on it.

Submitted means it's received and waiting to be picked up. Assigned means a department has taken it. In Progress means someone is actively working on it. Resolved means they've marked it fixed. Rejected means it was turned down, with a reason. Cancelled means you withdrew it.

An admin can reject a complaint, and they have to give a reason when they do — you'll see that reason on the complaint's detail screen. Common causes are duplicates of something already reported, or an issue outside the college's control.

q: how does it decide what is urgent
entries.a: The AI scores each complaint as Low, Medium, High or Critical from what you describe, the category and how urgent the wording sounds. Safety issues like exposed wiring rank Critical. If several people report the same thing, the original is bumped up in priority.

q: made a mistake in my complaint
entries.a: While a complaint is still 'Submitted' you can edit its description or cancel it from the complaint detail screen. Once a department has picked it up, it's locked so the record stays honest.

q: it was marked resolved but isnt fixed
they closed it but its not fixed
entries.a: If something is marked Resolved but isn't really fixed, rate it 2 stars or fewer when giving feedback and you'll be able to reopen it. It goes back to the department rather than being quietly closed.
Once a complaint is resolved you can rate the fix out of 5 stars and leave a short comment. Low ratings let you reopen the complaint, and the ratings feed the admin analytics.

q: how many complaints can i submit
entries.a: You can submit up to 5 complaints a day. It's a spam guard, not a judgement — if you genuinely hit it, wait until tomorrow or speak to the department directly.

Pick ಕನ್ನಡ or हिन्दी from the small script selector above the description box and type using your normal English keyboard — it converts as you go, so 'fan kelsa madtilla' becomes ಫ್ಯಾನ್ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡ್ತಿಲ್ಲ. It's phonetic, so type what you hear. You can also switch the whole app's language under Profile.
If you're offline when you submit, the complaint is queued on your phone and sent automatically once you're back on Wi-Fi or mobile data. You don't need to redo it.

q: ask a question about my complaint
entries.a: Each complaint has a comment thread. You and the handling department can post there, so you can add detail or answer a question without filing a new complaint. Comments can't be deleted once posted.

The system spots complaints that look like something reported in the last 24 hours and flags them as possible duplicates. Rather than dismissing yours, it raises the priority of the original — more reports means it gets treated as more urgent.
Yes — if you allow notifications, you'll be told when your complaint's status changes, such as when a department assigns it or marks it resolved.

Create an account with your name, department, role (student, faculty or staff), email and a password. If you forget your password, tap 'Forgot?' on the sign-in screen and you'll get a reset link by email. You stay signed in between visits.

Campus is divided into zones — Block A, Block B, Block C, Library, Canteen, Hostel, Parking and Grounds. The app detects your zone from GPS and preselects it, and you can change it from the dropdown if the problem is somewhere else.

Complaints are routed to the responsible department automatically — Facilities, Maintenance, Utilities, Infrastructure, Academic Office and so on. Department admins only see the complaints that belong to them.

Photo storage is currently switched off in this version, so complaints save without the image and show a category icon instead. The camera step still works. It's a hosting-plan limitation and can be switched back on without any app change.
